trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information: name with SSN, ID number, medical information, biometric data, or geolocation) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days only if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida individual by mail or email (English and Spanish templates)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - most associates, candidates, and clinicians are Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (record the time in the decision log)
owner: General Counsel with the Director of Compliance and Privacy

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement the firm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports it; unlikely when SSNs or bank data were taken
owner: General Counsel with the Director of Compliance and Privacy

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General) with the synopsis, count, services offered, notice copy, and contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (the associate register holds about 168,000 records)
owner: General Counsel with the Director of Compliance and Privacy

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000
owner: General Counsel with the Director of Compliance and Privacy

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request (may be extended or revoked in writing)
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the firm (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains the firm's personal information (payroll, ATS, timekeeping, credentialing, screening, VMS, contact center, AI vendors) has a breach of its system
deadline: Vendor must notify the firm as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination; the firm then gives notices under (3) and (4). Firm contracts require 72 hours (POL-01 4.9)
notify: The firm (Information Security Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - breach contact registered with each Tier 1 vendor (POAM-017)

citation: State breach notification statutes in each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Affected associates, candidates, or clinicians who live outside Florida (about 4% of associate records, mostly Alabama and Georgia addresses)
deadline: Varies by state; follow each state's law
notify: Residents and regulators as each state requires
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - run the residence-state report for every affected person
owner: General Counsel (outside counsel confirms each state)

citation: E-Verify MOU for Employers Art. II.A.16
trigger: Suspected or confirmed loss of control of, or unauthorized access to, E-Verify personal data (case data and results in the ATS I-9 module, or E-Verify credentials)
deadline: Immediately
notify: DHS E-Verify by phone (888-464-4218) or email (E-Verify@dhs.gov) with the subject "Privacy Incident - Password"
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the ATS I-9 module or an E-Verify account is involved

trigger: Security incident affecting MSP client data, VMS data, or contingent worker data in the program
deadline: Within 48 hours of confirming the incident (both MSP clients)
notify: Each MSP client's named security and program contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SYS-11, MSP timesheets, or payrolled worker data is involved
owner: Vice President, Managed Workforce Solutions with the General Counsel

obligation: Health care and other client contract notices
trigger: Security incident affecting client information (client contacts, timesheets, credential files shared through the client compliance portal)
deadline: Per contract (the largest clients require 72 hours)
notify: Client security contacts in the contract register
applies_at_this_tier: Only if client data is involved; associate-only data does not trigger most contracts

obligation: IRS notice of Form W-2 data loss (guidance)
citation: IRS guidance: Form W-2/SSN data theft information for businesses and payroll service providers
trigger: Theft of employee W-2 or SSN data
deadline: As soon as possible (the IRS may be able to protect employees from tax-related identity theft if told quickly)
notify: IRS at dataloss@irs.gov with the subject "W2 Data Loss" and a contact; do not attach employee personal information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended; the associate register includes SSNs and pay data

trigger: Suspected security incident or vendor outage that may lead to a claim
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier hotline before engaging incident response vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($5 million limit, $100,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

trigger: Funds lost to pay diversion or payment redirection
deadline: Per policy notice terms
notify: Crime carrier ($250,000 social engineering sublimit)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if diverted pay or payments are lost

trigger: Severity 1 incident or material disruption, including a missed or delayed payroll
deadline: Per credit agreement; sponsor operating partner informed within 24 hours (internal rule)
notify: Credit line agent bank; PE sponsor operating partner; audit committee chair
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Chief Executive Officer with the CFO

trigger: Payroll diversion, data theft, or extortion
deadline: As soon as possible (supports recovery of diverted funds and any 501.171(4)(b) delay request)
notify: FBI IC3 online report; local FBI field office
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is received and payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion occurs

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a covered entity
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: HIPAA covered entity client
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm is not a business associate for placement services (P03 G-152); recheck if a service involving PHI is added

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment report (proposed) - NOT YET IN EFFECT; final rule pending
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). As proposed, the firm would exceed its SBA size standard, but whether it is in a critical infrastructure sector is uncertain; counsel will assess any final rule

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article (Kaspersky) identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held
